title: Independently replay the P104 supplier, paired caller and terminal sink
body:
Independent source readers reproduce both BIT orientations, the complete rational operator and 13,030,044 basis products, and the actual 36/48-call signed invoices. The recorded 451-factor arithmetic and new compact caller are separately checked.

## Scope and source

Pins #7830, #7863, #7912 and the compact caller identities. The rational scalar and finite arithmetic check has the stated owned-erasure, stock, precision, compiler and recovery premises. The source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`. The included source manifest identifies every public dependency used.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-independent-caller-sink-replay/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory, check its checksum manifest, and run the extracted commands. All seven receipts reproduced byte for byte in a clean copy; the rational run took 15.42 seconds. Includes same-grade owner exchange, exact grid decrement and altered caller controls. Hosted execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Qualify changed physical banks and full application before transferring the finite conditions to a new layout.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. [Campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
